long_biography.plain_text:
Dhollander joined his parents' tail-lift business at eighteen and concentrated on its international development. With his sister Nancy, he became part of the second generation leading DHOLLANDIA. Together they expanded the Belgian family manufacturer into a vertically integrated business with production and service operations across multiple countries. His contribution was technical as well as managerial: patent records name him on several truck-loading and hydraulic-platform designs.

He continues to hold shareholder and management roles in the group's Central European manufacturing operation. DHOLLANDIA's core products are hydraulic tail lifts, column lifts and related loading systems for commercial vehicles, connecting Dhollander's wealth to specialised industrial manufacturing and active family-business stewardship. Company sales, factories and subsidiary assets remain enterprise measures rather than his personal property.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative input assigns person 7605 the 40.70-metre, 420-GT Andiamo. A registry-derived Malta record names the exact upstream-form JAN PRUDENCE J DHOLLANDER as shareholder of Andiamo One Marine Limited, and YachtBuyer independently matches the vessel's dimensions and Maltese flag. The public material does not itself reproduce the yacht registry or state that the company holds title, so the company evidence is treated as a strong collision-resolution bridge rather than standalone proof of beneficial ownership.

The owner input dates the relationship from 2023, while public yacht sources describe the SD132 as launched in late 2024 and delivered in 2025. The earlier date may reflect an order or build-period association. No correction is proposed because the dossier is not authorised to alter vessel relationships and the discrepancy does not change person identification.

Current Slovak official records and European Patent Office documents use Jan Prudence Jozef Dhollander, supporting expansion of the upstream abbreviation. Some Belgian patent records order the given names Jan Jozef Prudence. The current official corporate form and the existing Prudence J. sequence support Jan Prudence Jozef as the canonical display, while the alternative is retained as a search variant.

The upstream record gives Belgium as main residence, a 2006 Luxembourg deed gives a Belgian address and the 2024 Slovak record lists an address in Bytča. Public records do not establish whether the Slovak address is now primary or secondary residence, so neither residence field is changed.

Belgian trade material explicitly says Jan's parents founded DHOLLANDIA and that Jan and Nancy became the second-generation leaders who expanded it. This supports Inherited and expanded, but no reviewed source identifies the exact legal transfer date, inheritance vehicle or current parent-company percentages.

A specialist 2022 source reported equal sibling ownership of the Jana holding, while historical official records show Jan's interest in a U.K. subsidiary and current Slovak records show a local shareholding. These facts establish owner-operator materiality but do not justify treating every group company, factory, revenue figure, dividend or historical valuation as Jan's personal property or current net worth.

Manufacturing is used for both wealth creation and current primary industry because the family platform and current official role centre on lifting-equipment production. Operator captures sustained leadership, internationalisation and technical contribution; it does not erase inherited ownership, and Founder is excluded because his parents created the original company.

Two official records support 16 July 1965, and the Luxembourg journal supports Sint-Niklaas. The upstream July and 1965 values are therefore retained while birth_day and place_of_birth are proposed. No secondary nationality is documented.

No exact-person Forbes profile, verified personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or standalone personal website was found. Only DHOLLANDIA's official Company Website is proposed because its relationship to Jan's defining business is independently established.

Automotive components is the minimum useful approved active tag because DHOLLANDIA's defining products are truck- and van-mounted tail lifts and loading systems. Engineer, Inventor, Heavy equipment, Road freight and Manufacturing automation are omitted: the patents remain ordinary biography evidence, while the other tags would overstate occupation, customer industry, product category or business model.

The replacement biography removes changing revenue, company-count, country-count and factory-investment figures. Both biographies exclude yachts, personal lifestyle, family valuation, dividends, group assets as personal wealth and source/confidence narration. Nothing has been compiled, approved or applied.
